Subject: Post-demo: Prompt corpus intake & model fit recommendations for Acme Health

Hi Beth / Sam —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call highlights
- Use case: clinical triage assistant for inbound patient messages (classification -> suggested responses -> routing).
- Key constraints: PHI must never be exported to third-party analytics; redaction/PII rules need to be enforced at ingestion.
- Success metrics: 85% intent classification accuracy on triage labels; average response time < 150ms P50; maintain human-in-the-loop fallback for low-confidence cases.

What we need from Acme Health to run a model-fit eval
1) Prompt corpus: 200–500 representative inbound messages (de-identified if necessary) across channels (portal, email, SMS). Please include edge cases (ambiguous intent, multi-intent, misspellings).
2) Labeling guidance: mapping from message -> triage label + desired assistant output (short response + routing suggestion).
3) Any regulatory constraints or redaction rules we should apply before evaluation.

We attached a short CSV template (acme_prompt_collection_template.csv) to collect the prompts. If PHI is a blocker, one path is: you submit raw prompts to your S3 bucket and we run the eval inside your VPC private deployment; otherwise, de-identify locally and share the CSV over the Drive link below.

Preliminary model recommendations (high level)
- Redwood-Lite-7B-q8: lower latency, good for classification-first flow
- Redwood-13B-guardrails-q4: stronger instruction-following for suggested responses, better on hallucination metrics in our healthcare benchmarks

Next steps & owners
- Beth/Sam: upload sample prompts (or confirm VPC eval) by Thu 3/25 — Beth to confirm approach.
- Marissa: will prepare a short eval plan and run microbenchmarks once prompts received.
- Rishi: will scope redaction rules and provide a short checklist for PHI-safe ingestion.

I'll follow up with the eval plan and the short benchmark link. Thanks — appreciate the candid conversation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap. Couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) PHI & redaction: We cannot export any raw PHI outside our environment. We can either: 
   - Option A: De-identify locally (strip names, MRNs, dates) and share the de-id CSV.
   - Option B: Provide Redwood access to a read-only S3 bucket in our VPC and you run the eval there (preferred if you need context-sensitive tokens).

2) Prompt examples: I've pasted three anonymized, representative prompts below — this should illustrate the spectrum. We'll collect more and try to get to ~300 examples.

Example 1 (simple):
"I can't log into my portal. Can someone reset my password?"
Desired label: account_support
Desired assistant response: "I can help with that — please confirm your date of birth (MM/DD) and we'll proceed with account verification."

Example 2 (multi-intent):
"I've been feeling dizzy and my meds make me nauseous. Is this normal? Also, my appointment got cancelled — can I reschedule?"
Desired labels: symptom_triage; appointment_reschedule
Desired assistant response: "I'm sorry you're feeling unwell. For dizziness and medication side effects, please select 'Request clinician call' so we can triage. Would you like me to reschedule your appointment now?"

Example 3 (edge, misspellings):
"cant breethin, need help asap"
Desired label: urgent_symptom
Desired assistant response: "If you are having difficulty breathing, please call 911 or go to your nearest ER. Would you like me to call a clinician now?"

3) Timeline: We can compile an initial set by Fri 3/26. Option B (VPC eval) might take an extra week to set up.

We'll confirm which path by Tue 3/23.

Thanks — Beth
Beth Carter

Hi Beth —

Appreciate the examples, those are perfect. A few concrete notes from an evaluation & model-fit perspective: 

Evaluation plan (brief)
- Tier 1 (classification-only): run intent classification microbenchmarks across Redwood-Lite-7B-q8 and Redwood-13B-guardrails-q4 to measure intent accuracy and P95 latency.
- Tier 2 (generation + safety): run response-generation metrics (ROUGE/F1 for template match, hallucination checks) and safety filters on the generated outputs.
- Tier 3 (regression guardrails): use a holdout prompt set (50 edge cases) to detect quality regressions between model versions.

Model recommendations (specific)
- Redwood-Lite-7B-q8 (fast path): target when latency is primary; expected P50 ~ 90–130ms on our dedicated instance profile. Good for classification-first routing.
- Redwood-13B-guardrails-q4 (primary): stronger instruction following, fewer hallucinations in our healthcare suite; will be primary candidate for suggested-response generation.
- Fallback: Redwood-Tiny-2B (cost-saver) for non-clinical administrative routing.

Data handling & redaction checklist (short)
- Remove direct identifiers (names, MRNs, SSNs) from shareable CSV columns.
- Preserve clinical tokens that help intent (symptom words, medication names) but hash patient IDs if needed.
- If you choose VPC eval, we'll provide a small infra template and IAM role to run the harness inside your environment.

Links & artifacts
- Healthcare microbenchmark: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/healthcare-qa-v2
- Eval harness (rwi-eval-suite): https://redwood.ai/eval/rwi-eval-suite
- Drive folder for prompt uploads: https://drive.redwood.com/s/AcmeHealth/Shared/PromptSet

If you confirm Option B (VPC eval), Rishi and I will kick off the infra checklist and aim to have the first run in 7–10 business days after access is granted. Otherwise, once we have the de-id CSV, we'll run the pipeline in our Hosted eval environment and share the microbenchmark report within 48 hours.

I'll draft a short sample evaluation report template and share back to this thread.

Best,
Marissa Cole
